youtube.title: Why Costco Won't Raise Its $1.50 Hot Dog Price (Jim Sinegal's Rule)
youtube.description:
The Costco hot dog has cost $1.50 with a soda since 1985, and the company has refused to raise the price ever since. When an executive said the combo was losing money, co-founder Jim Sinegal reportedly told him to figure it out instead. Why would a company that took in $254 billion in a year guard one cheap lunch so fiercely, and what does the Costco food court really get from it?

This documentary follows the decision from Sol Price's first warehouse club in 1976 to Costco's 2024 membership fee rise. It covers the changes Costco made behind the counter, the rotisserie chicken that copied the playbook, the rival that undercut the price, and the membership fees equal to about two-thirds of its profit. Every figure is from Costco's filings or named reporting.

{CHAPTERS}
